title: Differentiated mosquito adaptive strategies underlie regional dominance of three ECSA sub-lineages in chikungunya virus

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) has emerged as a rapidly expanding global health threat and has been reported in 119 countries and territories, with recent outbreaks across Asia, Europe, and the Americas.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The East/Central/South African (ECSA) genotype has increasingly predominated in multiple regions, yet the molecular basis of its competitive advantage remains unresolved.
analysis.methods: Here, we demonstrate that three ECSA sub-lineages—ECSA-IOL, ECSA-2.1, and ECSA-2.2—have independently evolved distinct vector-associated evolutionary patterns that underlie their divergent geographic dominance.
analysis.main_results: Using comparative phylogenomic analyses of complete CHIKV genomes and selection pressure analyses (RELAX/BUSTED/Contrast-FEL), we found that ECSA-2.1 showed intensified selection on structural-protein genes and accumulated substitutions previously associated with Aedes aegypti , explaining its rapid displacement of the Asian genotype across the Americas.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Genome-wide analysis revealed lineage-characteristic and convergent substitutions, providing molecular signatures associated with ECSA competitive advantage.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest vector niche partitioning as an important driver of CHIKV global expansion dynamics, with potential implications for outbreak forecasting, vector control prioritization, and the design of broadly protective vaccines.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations or evidence strength assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the molecular basis of the competitive advantage of the East/Central/South African (ECSA) genotype of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) across different regions. The research highlights that three ECSA sub-lineages—ECSA-IOL, ECSA-2.1, and ECSA-2.2—have evolved distinct vector-associated evolutionary patterns, which explain their divergent geographic dominance. The study employed comparative phylogenomic analyses and selection pressure analyses to identify substitutions in structural-protein genes of ECSA-2.1 that are linked to Aedes aegypti, contributing to its displacement of the Asian genotype in the Americas. Additionally, genome-wide analysis revealed lineage-specific and convergent substitutions, offering molecular signatures for ECSA's competitive advantage. The findings suggest that vector niche partitioning plays a significant role in CHIKV's global expansion, with implications for outbreak forecasting, vector control, and vaccine development. The study does not explicitly report limitations or evidence strength assessment.

title: Nanopore Sequencing for Chikungunya Virus: Principles and Application.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the application of nanopore sequencing in Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genomics, addressing the need for rapid, portable, and accurate methods to track viral diversity and evolution during outbreaks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on the principles and application of nanopore sequencing for Chikungunya virus, examining its use in clinical and vector samples to recover complete genomes and monitor viral spread.
analysis.methods: Nanopore sequencing was used to directly sequence RNA and DNA by measuring ionic current changes as nucleic acids pass through nanoscale pores, enabling real-time, single-molecule analysis of Chikungunya virus genomes without the need for culture.
analysis.main_results: The method demonstrated the ability to rapidly recover full viral genomes from clinical and vector samples, facilitating real-time tracking of viral diversity, evolution, and spread during outbreaks.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as a significant advancement in pathogen surveillance, particularly for resource-limited settings, where nanopore sequencing provides a flexible and powerful tool for monitoring Chikungunya virus.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more effective genomic surveillance strategies for Chikungunya virus, enhancing outbreak response and epidemic preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges challenges in basecalling and error correction but highlights robust quality control pipelines that ensure reliable results, supporting a moderate confidence in the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the application of nanopore sequencing in Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genomics, emphasizing its advantages in real-time, portable, and long-read analysis. The research highlights how nanopore sequencing enables rapid, culture-independent recovery of complete CHIKV genomes from clinical and vector samples, facilitating real-time tracking of viral diversity and spread. The authors interpret these findings as a significant advancement in pathogen surveillance, particularly for resource-limited settings, where the method offers flexibility and power. The study notes challenges in basecalling and error correction but underscores the reliability of quality control pipelines. These results have implications for improving genomic surveillance and epidemic preparedness for CHIKV. The evidence is considered moderate in strength due to the acknowledged limitations in the sequencing process, though the method's potential is well-supported by prior experiences with other pathogens.

title: Accounting for heterogeneity in mosquito exposure to forecast chikungunya outbreaks in Reunion Island and Paraguay: a mathematical modelling study

analysis.research_question_and_background: We aimed to assess whether accounting for heterogeneity in mosquito exposure improves the ability of transmission models to reproduce past chikungunya outbreaks and to forecast an ongoing outbreak in real time.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We extended an existing transmission model, originally developed to forecast dengue outbreaks in Reunion Island and incorporating seasonality, to include heterogeneity in mosquito exposure.
analysis.methods: We compared this model to versions assuming homogeneous exposure, evaluating their ability to reproduce the 2005-06 Reunion Island outbreak and the 2023 Paraguay Metropolitana subregion outbreak.
analysis.main_results: Homogeneity models either overestimated final seroprevalence (80% vs 38% observed) or required a reduction of approximately 50% in the basic reproduction number following interventions, which is implausible.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These results highlight how incorporating heterogeneity in mosquito exposure can improve chikungunya outbreaks forecasting.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: FUNDING: EU; Laboratoire d'Excellence Integrative Biology of Emerging Infectious Diseases programme; Agence Nationale de Recherches Sur le Sida, les Hépatites Virales et les Maladies Infectieuses Émergentes; Agence Nationale de la Recherche.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: A post-outbreak serosurvey indicated that the heterogeneity model underestimated final seroprevalence (46·1% vs 61·6% observed), whereas the homogeneity model overestimated final seroprevalence (78·5%), suggesting that heterogeneity in 2025 might have been lower than that in 2005-06.

analysis.summary_en: We aimed to assess whether accounting for heterogeneity in mosquito exposure improves the ability of transmission models to reproduce past chikungunya outbreaks and to forecast an ongoing outbreak in real time. We extended an existing transmission model, originally developed to forecast dengue outbreaks in Reunion Island and incorporating seasonality, to include heterogeneity in mosquito exposure. We compared this model to versions assuming homogeneous exposure, evaluating their ability to reproduce the 2005-06 Reunion Island outbreak and the 2023 Paraguay Metropolitana subregion outbreak. Homogeneity models either overestimated final seroprevalence (80% vs 38% observed) or required a reduction of approximately 50% in the basic reproduction number following interventions, which is implausible. These results highlight how incorporating heterogeneity in mosquito exposure can improve chikungunya outbreaks forecasting. FUNDING: EU; Laboratoire d'Excellence Integrative Biology of Emerging Infectious Diseases programme; Agence Nationale de Recherches Sur le Sida, les Hépatites Virales et les Maladies Infectieuses Émergentes; Agence Nationale de la Recherche. A post-outbreak serosurvey indicated that the heterogeneity model underestimated final seroprevalence (46·1% vs 61·6% observed), whereas the homogeneity model overestimated final seroprevalence (78·5%), suggesting that heterogeneity in 2025 might have been lower than that in 2005-06.

title: Overview of Chikungunya Virus Epidemiology, Biology, and Pathogenesis.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus within the Togaviridae family, is transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The virus causes an acute febrile illness characterized by severe, often bilateral polyarthralgia, with potential progression to chronic musculoskeletal pain and rare systemic complications involving cardiovascular and neurological systems.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study provides an overview of Chikungunya virus epidemiology, biology, and pathogenesis. It includes information on the virus's structure, replication mechanisms, and its global spread. The analysis covers CHIKV lineages and their associated diseases.
analysis.methods: CHIKV exhibits a spherical, enveloped virion (~70 nm) with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry, incorporating E1/E2 glycoprotein heterodimers that mediate receptor binding and membrane fusion. Its positive-sense RNA genome (~11.8 kb) encodes nonstructural proteins for replication and structural proteins for virion assembly. Replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving synthesis of genomic and subgenomic RNAs, followed by glycoprotein maturation and budding at the plasma membrane.
analysis.main_results: Since introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence remains high, with >180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Epidemiologically, CHIKV has expanded beyond Africa and Asia, with major outbreaks driven by adaptive mutations enhancing transmission via A. Preventive strategies rely on vector control and vaccination; VLP-based vaccines (e.g., Vimkunya) show promise, while live-attenuated formulations face safety concerns.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: No licensed antivirals exist; current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study provides an overview of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) epidemiology, biology, and pathogenesis. It describes the virus as an arthropod-borne alphavirus transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, causing acute febrile illness with severe polyarthralgia and potential chronic complications. The virus has a spherical, enveloped virion with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry and a positive-sense RNA genome encoding replication and structural proteins. CHIKV replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving genomic and subgenomic RNA synthesis, glycoprotein maturation, and budding at the plasma membrane. Since its introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence has remained high, with over 180,000 confirmed cases in 2025. The study highlights the expansion of CHIKV beyond Africa and Asia, driven by adaptive mutations that enhance transmission. Preventive strategies rely on vector control and vaccination, with VLP-based vaccines showing promise and live-attenuated formulations facing safety concerns. No licensed antivirals exist, and current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development. The evidence is general and does not include specific limitations or evidence strength assessments.

title: Successful use of a Janus-kinase (JAK) inhibitor in chronic chikungunya arthritis refractory to conventional synthetic DMARDs: a case report

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limited treatment options for chronic chikungunya arthritis refractory to conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case report of a 50-year-old Brazilian woman with serologically confirmed chikungunya virus infection and chronic chikungunya arthritis was described.
analysis.methods: The patient was initially managed with symptomatic analgesics, prednisone, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, and leflunomide, but these were discontinued due to adverse effects or lack of efficacy.
analysis.main_results: Baricitinib (4 mg/day), a Janus kinase inhibitor, was initiated, resulting in marked clinical and laboratory improvement, including a decrease in disease activity score, normalisation of C-reactive protein, and resolution of morning stiffness.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The case suggests that Janus kinase inhibition may be a therapeutic option for selected patients with chronic chikungunya arthritis refractory to conventional treatment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This case highlights the potential of Janus kinase inhibitors as a novel treatment for chronic chikungunya arthritis, which can inform future studies and clinical practice.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its case report design, which does not allow for generalisation of findings. The patient's response may not be representative of the broader population.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a patient with chronic chikungunya arthritis who achieved marked clinical and laboratory improvement with the Janus kinase inhibitor baricitinib, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic option for refractory cases.

title: Protocol for Detecting and Sequencing Chikungunya Virus from Field-Collected Mosquitoes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Arboviral diseases represent a major public health challenge, especially in tropical regions where environmental conditions may favor the proliferation and spread of mosquito vectors. Thus, early and accurate detection of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in mosquito populations can be a valuable tool for effective surveillance of circulating variants and for identifying new viral introductions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The supplied evidence does not report details of the study design, setting, dates, or population.
analysis.methods: Given the challenges of detecting arboviruses in field-captured mosquitoes, we describe an integrated workflow for CHIKV molecular detection and whole-genome sequencing. This protocol includes mosquito homogenization using a bead-based mechanical disruptor, RNA extraction using TRIzol reagent with minor modifications, molecular screening using CHIKV-specific RT-qPCR, and whole-genome amplification followed by sequencing on Illumina platforms.
analysis.main_results: The supplied evidence does not report any observed results.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The supplied evidence does not report any interpretation or novelty statements.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The supplied evidence does not report any implications for surveillance, diagnosis, treatment, vaccination, ecology, risk assessment, prevention or future study.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report any limitations or assessment of evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This protocol outlines a comprehensive workflow for detecting and sequencing chikungunya virus (CHIKV) from field-collected mosquitoes, addressing the public health need for early surveillance of arboviral threats in tropical regions. The authors describe a bead-based mechanical disruption for mosquito homogenization, followed by TRIzol-based RNA extraction with minor modifications. CHIKV-specific RT-qPCR is employed for molecular screening, and positive samples undergo whole-genome amplification and Illumina sequencing to recover complete viral genomes. Although the protocol is optimized for individual mosquitoes and yields high-quality RNA suitable for both entomological surveillance and genomic analysis, the study does not provide empirical results, interpretations, or assessments of limitations. Consequently, the evidence base remains limited to methodological description, underscoring the need for future validation studies to confirm the protocol’s effectiveness and applicability in diverse field settings.

title: Global patterns of genetic diversity and evolution in chikungunya virus E2 glycoprotein

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the genetic diversity and evolution of the E2 glycoprotein in chikungunya virus (CHIKV), focusing on its role in host-cell attachment, immune recognition, and lineage diversification. The E2 glycoprotein is a key antigenic determinant that influences viral evolution and epidemic dynamics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study conducted a comprehensive analysis of E2 genetic diversity using a dataset of sequences collected across regions, hosts, and epidemic periods. Population structure analyses using Fst indicated significant genetic differentiation between regional populations, reflecting restricted gene flow and localized evolutionary trajectories.
analysis.methods: The study applied diversity indices, neutrality tests, and haplotypes network analysis to characterize evolutionary pressures acting on the E2 glycoprotein. To assess the influence of geography, host, and time on viral population structure, spatial–temporal stratification and analysis were performed using Fixation index test (Fst).
analysis.main_results: Nucleotide diversity varied considerably across time, with the pre-expansion period (pre-2004) showing the highest diversity (Pi = 0.085), while more recent outbreak periods exhibited comparatively reduced diversity (Pi = 0.012). Neutrality tests revealed signatures of both purifying and positive selection across the three CHIKV E2 lineages, supported by codon-based analyses showing pervasive purifying constraint but recurrent diversifying signals at lineage-specific sites.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the spatiotemporal evolution of CHIKV E2 glycoprotein, emphasizing its role in viral adaptation and immune evasion. These results provide novel insights into the evolutionary pressures shaping CHIKV lineages and their implications for immune recognition and epidemic dynamics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study's results can inform surveillance strategies for CHIKV by highlighting the genetic diversity patterns and evolutionary pressures that may influence viral adaptation and immune evasion. This knowledge is crucial for understanding the potential for immune escape and developing targeted interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is based on a comprehensive dataset, but the analysis of genetic diversity and evolutionary pressures is limited by the availability of sequences and the potential for geographic and temporal biases. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on existing sequence data and the absence of direct experimental validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the genetic diversity and evolution of the E2 glycoprotein in chikungunya virus (CHIKV), focusing on its role in host-cell attachment, immune recognition, and lineage diversification. Using a dataset of sequences collected across regions, hosts, and epidemic periods, the research applied diversity indices, neutrality tests, and haplotype network analysis to characterize evolutionary pressures. Results showed that nucleotide diversity was highest in the pre-expansion period (Pi = 0.085) and lower in more recent outbreaks (Pi = 0.012). Neutrality tests indicated both purifying and positive selection across CHIKV E2 lineages, with lineage-specific diversifying signals observed at key codons. These findings underscore the spatiotemporal evolution of CHIKV E2 and its implications for viral adaptation and immune evasion. The study's evidence is moderate in strength due to reliance on existing sequence data and potential biases, but it provides valuable insights for understanding CHIKV evolution and informing surveillance strategies.

title: Tactical Paralysis: The Interplay Between Chikungunya Virus and Host Mitochondrial Dynamics in Immune Evasion and Metabolic Remodeling

analysis.scope_and_question: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an expanding alphavirus causing acute febrile illness, yet its most debilitating signature remains the refractory chronic arthralgia persisting for months or years.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This review deconstructs the tactical paralysis of host mitochondrial dynamics driven by CHIKV. We delineate how specific viral components (nsP2, TF, and 6K) act as molecular wedges or post-translational modifiers that hijack host fission/fusion machinery (Drp1/Mfn2), driving the mitochondrial network into compulsive fragmentation.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Crucially, this morphological collapse operates as a double-edged sword: in the acute phase, it disrupts the MAVS signalosome to mute the type I interferon response; in the chronic phase, it cascades into a profound immunometabolic rewiring within the synovial microenvironment.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: In synovial macrophages, mitochondrial fragmentation ruptures the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, causing succinate accumulation that epigenetically locks cells into a persistent, pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype, establishing a destructive "metabolic memory." Concurrently, in fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS), retrograde signaling from mitochondrial ROS and cytosolic mtDNA leakage prompts a pseudo-malignant transformation, accelerating extracellular matrix degradation via MMP-13 and RANKL hyperactivation.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: By integrating these dimensions, we provide a unified framework for CHIKV chronicity and propose targeted mitochondrial quality control as a high-value therapeutic frontier to break post-viral arthropathy.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in causing chronic arthralgia through its manipulation of host mitochondrial dynamics. The study highlights how viral components such as nsP2, TF, and 6K interfere with mitochondrial fission and fusion processes, leading to fragmentation. This fragmentation serves dual purposes: it suppresses the type I interferon response during the acute phase and initiates immunometabolic rewiring in the chronic phase. The review identifies specific mechanisms, including the disruption of the TCA cycle in macrophages and the activation of MMP-13 and RANKL in fibroblast-like synoviocytes, which contribute to persistent inflammation and extracellular matrix degradation. The findings suggest that targeting mitochondrial quality control could offer a promising therapeutic approach for managing post-viral arthropathy. The review emphasizes the need for further research into these mechanisms to develop effective interventions.

title: Assessing the Vector Competence for Chikungunya Virus in Mosquitoes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a human pathogenic, mosquito‐borne arbovirus causing epidemic outbreaks across Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Americas, highlighting a need to understand its transmission dynamics.

analysis.methods: The authors outline protocols for preparing Aedes aegypti mosquitoes for infection with freshly cultivated CHIKV and for detecting virus in mosquitoes using plaque assays and amplification of saliva samples in cell culture.
analysis.main_results: The supplied evidence does not report any experimental results or quantitative findings.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The development of novel approaches to prevent mosquito transmission of the virus in the field requires a detailed study of CHIKV interactions with its mosquito vectors in the laboratory.

analysis.summary_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a globally emerging arbovirus responsible for widespread human outbreaks, prompting investigation into its mosquito transmission. The chapter describes laboratory methods for infecting Aedes aegypti mosquitoes with freshly cultured CHIKV and for assessing viral presence using plaque assays and saliva amplification in cell culture. While the authors emphasize that detailed vector‐virus interaction studies are essential for developing novel transmission‐blocking strategies, the provided excerpt contains no information on study design, participant or mosquito cohorts, experimental results, or public‐health implications. Consequently, the evidence base is limited to methodological outlines without reported outcomes or identified limitations, yielding a low confidence assessment of the overall findings.

title: Chikungunya Virus Infection of Monocytes Generates a Persistent Macrophage Reservoir That Promotes IFN-π/IL-27–STAT1- and NF-κB–Driven Chronic Arthritis

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand whether Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection of monocytes drives their differentiation into macrophages, which could sustain chronic inflammation and arthritis. This addresses the knowledge gap in understanding the mechanisms behind chronic CHIKV arthritis, a significant public health concern.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized a combination of pediatric CHIKV patient samples, in vitro differentiation of primary human monocytes, and single-cell RNA-sequencing of joint-associated macrophages from an immunocompetent mouse model of chronic CHIKV arthritis.
analysis.methods: Monocytes were isolated from CHIKV patients and infected in vitro to differentiate into macrophages. Transcriptomic profiling and single-cell RNA-sequencing were performed to analyze gene expression patterns and identify key signaling pathways.

title: Naked-Eye Visual Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification Method for the Rapid Detection of Chikungunya Virus.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) represents a significant global health threat due to its recent resurgence, and this study aimed to develop a rapid detection protocol using capillary-modified visual loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP).

analysis.main_results: The LAMP assay produced a distinct yellowish-green color change indicating CHIKV presence, demonstrating the effectiveness and simplicity of the protocol.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the LAMP protocol offers a rapid, simple diagnostic tool for CHIKV, highlighting its potential for timely public health interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The rapid, visual LAMP assay could improve CHIKV surveillance and outbreak response by providing point-of-care detection in resource-limited settings.

Researchers established an in vitro protocol using Vero cells to propagate CHIKV, extracted viral RNA with the MolPure kit, and performed loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) at 63 °C for 25 minutes. Detection relied on a distinct yellowish-green color change, confirming CHIKV presence and demonstrating the assay’s simplicity and effectiveness. The authors interpret this as a promising rapid diagnostic tool that could enable timely public health interventions. title: Expression and Purification of nsP2 Protease of Chikungunya Virus.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop a method for expressing and purifying the nsP2 protease of Chikungunya virus, which is essential for viral replication and polyprotein processing.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study describes a protocol for the heterologous expression and purification of CHIKV nsP2 protease domain in Escherichia coli, focusing on the protein's production and isolation.
analysis.methods: The nsP2 protease domain was expressed at low temperature as a His-tagged construct and purified under native conditions using immobilized metal ion affinity chromatography, followed by dialysis for buffer exchange.
analysis.main_results: The procedure typically yields milligram quantities of highly pure (>95%) and active nsP2pro, and has been successfully applied to wild-type and mutant variants for enzymatic assays and inhibitor screening.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The described method provides a reliable and straightforward approach for obtaining active nsP2pro, which is valuable for further biochemical and structural studies.

The protocol involves expressing the protein at low temperature as a His-tagged construct and purifying it under native conditions using immobilized metal ion affinity chromatography, followed by dialysis for buffer exchange. title: Determination of Chikungunya Virus Infectious Titer Using Plaque Assays.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to establish a reliable method for quantifying infectious chikungunya virus particles in cell culture supernatants.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study describes a plaque-forming assay protocol to measure infectious viral particles in cell culture supernatants, with no specific population or sample size mentioned.
analysis.methods: The plaque-forming assay is described as the gold-standard method for measuring infectious viral particles, where lytic viruses infect and destroy host cells, but their spread is restricted by a viscous overlay medium.
analysis.main_results: The number of plaques formed in the assay reflects the number of infectious viral particles initially present in the sample and is reported as plaque-forming units (PFU) per sample volume.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the plaque-forming assay as a direct and accurate method for quantifying infectious chikungunya virus particles, providing a standardized approach for virological analysis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a reliable method for quantifying infectious chikungunya virus particles, which is essential for virological surveillance and understanding viral load dynamics in outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to describing the method without reporting specific results, but the evidence is strong as it outlines the gold-standard technique for measuring infectious viral particles.

analysis.summary_en: This study outlines the plaque-forming assay as the gold-standard method for measuring infectious chikungunya virus particles in cell culture supernatants. The technique involves infecting host cells with lytic viruses, which are restricted by a viscous overlay medium, leading to localized clear areas known as plaques. The number of plaques is used to quantify the initial viral particle count and is reported as plaque-forming units (PFU) per sample volume. The authors interpret the assay as a direct and accurate method for determining viral infectivity, which has significant implications for virological surveillance and understanding viral load dynamics. The study provides a detailed protocol for performing the assay but does not report specific results, which limits its evidence strength to a moderate level.

title: A-083 Rapid screening for acute chikungunya virus infection using an interpretable machine learning model based on routine complete blood count parameters.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The 2025 Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) outbreak in Foshan, China, highlighted an urgent need for rapid screening tools. Molecular diagnostics are constrained by time, cost, and availability.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 1,537 suspected CHIKV patients from two medical centers in Foshan. CHIKV infection was confirmed by reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR).
analysis.methods: CBC and cell population data (CPD) were obtained using Mindray BC-7500 analyzers. After rigorous data preprocessing and feature selection using LASSO regression, four models Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and LightGBM (LGBM) were developed on a training set (n=1,132 from Center A) and evaluated on an internal test set (n=192) and an independent external test set (n=213 from Center B).
analysis.main_results: In the external validation set, the LR model demonstrated superior and robust performance (AUC = 0.807, sensitivity = 88.0%, specificity = 65.0%, NPV = 93.0%), significantly outperforming the tree-based models. Decision curve analysis confirmed its clinical utility across a wide range of risk thresholds.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: SHAP analysis revealed that lower white blood cell count (WBC_N), lower lymphocyte percentage (Lym%), and increased neutrophil morphological heterogeneity (D_Neu_SSC_CV) were the strongest predictors, aligning with the established pathophysiology of CHIKV infection. This model serves as a reliable, rapid, and cost-effective tool for patient triage during outbreaks, especially in resource-limited settings awaiting confirmatory PCR testing.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the LR model can be used for rapid screening of acute CHIKV infection, which is critical for timely diagnosis and management during outbreaks. This could improve patient triage and resource allocation in resource-limited settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on retrospective data, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate due to the limited generalizability of the results and the absence of prospective validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning model using routine complete blood count (CBC) parameters to identify patients at high risk of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection. The model was developed and validated using data from 1,537 suspected CHIKV patients across two medical centers in Foshan, China. The LR model demonstrated superior performance in the external validation set, with an AUC of 0.807, sensitivity of 88.0%, specificity of 65.0%, and NPV of 93.0%. SHAP analysis identified key predictors such as lower white blood cell count and increased neutrophil morphological heterogeneity. The model is proposed as a reliable, rapid, and cost-effective tool for patient triage during CHIKV outbreaks, particularly in resource-limited settings. However, the study is based on retrospective data, which may limit its generalizability and evidence strength, assessed as moderate.

title: Surgery as a Management Option for Post-Chikungunya Chronic Synovitis Presenting as a Dorsal Wrist Mass

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the need to explore management options for post-Chikungunya chronic synovitis presenting as a dorsal wrist mass, given the rarity of such presentations and the lack of established treatment protocols.

analysis.methods: The case was reported based on clinical presentation, imaging, and histopathological findings.
analysis.main_results: Imaging demonstrated inflammatory synovitis and extensor tenosynovitis, confirmed by histopathology as chronic inflammatory synovitis. Despite conservative treatment, the patient developed significant functional limitations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that post-Chikungunya chronic synovitis results from persistent immune-mediated inflammation, and that surgery may be indicated in selected cases with localized disease and functional impairment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This case highlights surgery as a valuable management option for localized post-Chikungunya chronic synovitis presenting as a dorsal wrist mass, emphasizing the need for individualized treatment approaches.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its case report design, which does not allow for generalization of the findings. The evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of randomized controlled trials or large-scale studies.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 40-year-old female with a progressively enlarging dorsal wrist mass following Chikungunya infection. Imaging and histopathology confirmed chronic inflammatory synovitis, and surgery was performed. The authors suggest that surgery may be a valuable management option for localized post-Chikungunya chronic synovitis.

title: Co-Infection of Dengue, Chikungunya, and West Nile Viruses Among Suspected Febrile Patients in Hodeidah Governorate, Yemen: A Retrospective Laboratory-Based Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Arboviral infections have emerged as a significant public health challenge worldwide, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions where environmental conditions support the establishment and expansion of competent mosquito vectors.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective laboratory-based study investigated co-infections of dengue, chikungunya, and West Nile viruses among suspected febrile patients in Hodeidah Governorate, Yemen.
analysis.methods: The study utilized laboratory-based testing to identify viral infections in suspected febrile patients, focusing on the detection of dengue virus (DENV), chikungunya virus (CHIKV), and West Nile virus (WNV) through molecular and serological assays.
analysis.main_results: The study found that co-infections of dengue, chikungunya, and West Nile viruses occurred among suspected febrile patients in Hodeidah Governorate, Yemen.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the potential for co-circulation of these arboviruses in the region, which may complicate surveillance and diagnosis efforts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results underscore the importance of integrated surveillance systems to detect and manage co-infections, which can have significant implications for public health strategies in endemic areas.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and based on laboratory data, which may limit its ability to establish causal relationships or provide real-time insights, resulting in moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective laboratory-based study in Hodeidah Governorate, Yemen, investigated co-infections of dengue, chikungunya, and West Nile viruses among suspected febrile patients. The research highlights the growing public health challenge posed by arboviruses, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions where mosquito vectors are prevalent. The study used molecular and serological assays to detect viral infections, revealing instances of co-infection among patients. These findings suggest the potential for co-circulation of these viruses in the region, which may complicate surveillance and diagnosis. The study's retrospective nature and reliance on laboratory data limit its ability to establish causal relationships, resulting in moderate confidence in the results. The results have important implications for public health strategies, emphasizing the need for integrated surveillance systems to address the complexities of arbovirus co-infections. The evidence is based on laboratory testing and does not include detailed statistical analyses or long-term follow-up.

title: Manifestaciones clínico-dermatológicas de la chikungunya: puntos clave para el internista, lecciones del brote en Cuba

analysis.research_question_and_background: La presente revisión narrativa busca identificar las manifestaciones clínico-dermatológicas de la fiebre chikungunya con relevancia para el internista, a partir del brote epidémico ocurrido en Cuba durante 2025.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Se consultaron artículos publicados entre 2008 y 2026 en PubMed/MEDLINE, SciELO y repositorios oficiales de la OPS/OMS, priorizándose revisiones sistemáticas, guías clínicas y series de casos.
analysis.methods: La chikungunya cursó con tres fases clínicas.
analysis.main_results: En la fase aguda predominaron la fiebre elevada, las poliartralgias severas simétricas y el exantema maculopapular.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Se identificaron manifestaciones cutáneo-mucosas distintivas como la hiperpigmentación centrofacial, las úlceras genitales, las lesiones vesículo-ampollosas en niños y la exacerbación de dermatosis preexistentes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Hasta el 60% de los casos evoluciona a la cronicidad, caracterizada por artritis inflamatoria persistente.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: La integración del binomio clínico-dermatológico constituye una herramienta fundamental para el diagnóstico diferencial frente a otras arbovirosis y para la identificación de pacientes con riesgo de cronicidad articular.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a narrative review of the clinical and dermatological manifestations of chikungunya, focusing on key findings relevant to internists, based on the 2025 epidemic in Cuba. The review analyzed articles published between 2008 and 2026 from PubMed/MEDLINE, SciELO, and official repositories of the WHO. The chikungunya virus was reported to progress through three clinical phases, with acute symptoms including high fever, severe symmetric polyarthritis, and maculopapular rash. Distinct cutaneous and mucosal manifestations were identified, such as centrofacial hyperpigmentation, genital ulcers, vesiculopustular lesions in children, and exacerbation of pre-existing dermatoses. The study highlights that up to 60% of cases evolve into chronicity, characterized by persistent inflammatory arthritis. The integration of clinical and dermatological features is emphasized as a critical tool for differential diagnosis and identifying patients at risk for chronic joint complications. The evidence is based on a comprehensive literature search, but the study does not provide detailed statistical analyses or experimental data, limiting the strength of the conclusions.

title: Insecticide resistance in Aedes aegypti across sub-Saharan Africa: An overview and perspectives for effective arbovirus control.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on insecticide resistance in Aedes aegypti across sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in relation to arboviruses such as chikungunya virus, with an emphasis on the public health implications of resistance for arbovirus control.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review searched bibliographic databases for studies published between January 2010 and December 2023. It identified 40 studies from 18 of 47 countries in sub-Saharan Africa, examining the distribution and molecular evidence of insecticide resistance in Aedes aegypti.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Insecticide resistance in Aedes aegypti is widespread and increasing in sub-Saharan Africa, with resistance to DDT and pyrethroids reported in multiple studies across West and Central Africa. Molecular investigations have identified five kdr mutations in 12 countries, while metabolic resistance mechanisms involving cytochrome P450s, carboxylesterases, and glutathione S-transferases have been reported in fewer studies.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence base is geographically uneven and limited for several insecticide classes and resistance mechanisms. Limited assessment of larvicides, emerging adulticide options, resistance intensity, and Aedes-targeted vector control interventions remains a significant gap.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Systematic and standardized insecticide resistance surveillance across sub-Saharan Africa is needed to address the growing public health concern posed by arboviruses such as chikungunya virus. Insecticide-based strategies remain essential for arbovirus control, but their effectiveness is threatened by increasing resistance.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines insecticide resistance in Aedes aegypti across sub-Saharan Africa, with a focus on its implications for arbovirus control, particularly for chikungunya virus. The evidence base includes 40 studies from 18 countries, highlighting resistance to DDT and pyrethroids in multiple regions and the identification of five kdr mutations in 12 countries. However, the review notes significant geographic unevenness in the evidence and identifies key knowledge gaps, including limited larvicide assessments and emerging adulticide options. The findings underscore the need for more systematic and standardized resistance surveillance to improve vector control strategies and mitigate the public health risks associated with arboviruses like chikungunya.

title: Congenital Arboviruses: A Review.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on congenital arboviruses, specifically Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), and addresses its impact on fetal development, transmission mechanisms, and clinical outcomes. The central question is to understand the epidemiology, pathogenesis, and diagnostic challenges of CHIKV-related congenital infections.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature on CHIKV and related congenital arboviruses. It includes epidemiological data, clinical case reports, and diagnostic studies, but does not explicitly report on meta-analysis or systematic review methodologies. The review does not specify databases or search dates, and eligibility criteria are not detailed.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that vertical transmission of CHIKV can occur, leading to congenital infections with potential adverse effects on fetal development. It highlights that inflammation, placental disruption, and viral replication in fetal tissues are common pathological features across arboviruses, including CHIKV.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that early diagnosis of CHIKV-related congenital infections is challenging due to overlapping clinical symptoms and limited laboratory capacity in endemic areas. Additionally, cross-reactivity in serological tests for flaviviruses complicates accurate detection. There is a lack of comprehensive data on long-term outcomes and specific maternal-fetal interactions unique to CHIKV.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for improved surveillance systems, targeted diagnostic tools, and preventive strategies such as vector control and maternal vaccination to reduce the burden of congenital CHIKV infections. It also underscores the importance of understanding maternal-fetal dynamics to develop effective public health interventions.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the impact of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) on fetal development, focusing on vertical transmission, pathogenesis, and diagnostic challenges. It highlights the common pathological features among arboviruses, including inflammation and placental disruption, and identifies gaps in understanding long-term outcomes. The review calls for enhanced surveillance, improved diagnostics, and preventive measures like vector control and maternal vaccination to mitigate the burden of congenital CHIKV infections. It also stresses the need for further research into maternal-fetal interactions to inform public health strategies.

title: A generalized lineage nomenclature for viral genomic epidemiology.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for a scalable and adaptable nomenclature system to effectively communicate viral diversity in the context of outbreak response and surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study generalized the principles of the Pango lineage system to create a framework for virus surveillance, focusing on chikungunya virus and its lineages.

analysis.main_results: The framework was applied to chikungunya virus, resulting in the designation of 21 lineages across 8 founding lineages, providing an alternative to the geography-based clade system.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as a novel approach to viral lineage classification that enhances the scalability and adaptability of genomic surveillance systems.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings offer a foundation for improved genomic surveillance of chikungunya virus and other pathogens, supporting more effective outbreak response and tracking.

title: Solanaceae-Derived Spirostane Saponins Inhibit Dengue Virus Replication and Viral Protein Expression and Exhibit Activity Against Multiple Arboviruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of specific antiviral therapies for mosquito-borne arboviruses, including chikungunya virus, by exploring novel compounds from plant sources.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed a bioactivity-guided approach to screen methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species for antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells, with a focus on chikungunya virus.
analysis.methods: The researchers used bioactivity-guided screening, fractionation, and purification techniques to isolate compounds, followed by structural characterization using UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy, and functional assays to assess antiviral activity.
analysis.main_results: Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Four spirostane-type steroidal saponins were isolated and demonstrated antiviral activity against DENV-2.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that spirostane saponins could serve as promising antiviral scaffolds, offering potential for the development of broad-spectrum antiviral agents against multiple arboviruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide a foundation for further research into plant-derived compounds as therapeutic options for chikungunya virus and other related arboviruses, potentially contributing to surveillance and treatment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro findings and does not address in vivo efficacy or clinical translation, which reduces the strength of the evidence to moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the potential of Solanaceae-derived spirostane saponins as antiviral agents against chikungunya virus and other arboviruses. The research highlights the growing global health burden of mosquito-borne viruses, including chikungunya, and the lack of specific therapies. A bioactivity-guided approach was used to screen extracts from eight Solanaceae species, identifying compounds that inhibit DENV-2 replication in Vero cells. Structural characterization and functional assays confirmed the antiviral activity of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, with evidence suggesting their efficacy against multiple arboviruses. The findings indicate that these compounds could be promising scaffolds for developing broad-spectrum antiviral agents. However, the study is limited to in vitro results, which restricts the strength of the evidence to moderate. The results may inform future research into plant-derived therapies for chikungunya and related viruses, contributing to surveillance and treatment strategies.

title: A case for eliminating Widal testing for enteric fever, India.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study argues for eliminating inaccurate serological tests, particularly the Widal test, for enteric fever in India due to its role in contributing to antimicrobial resistance and poor disease surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective audit of 100 febrile children at a New Delhi tertiary hospital found that, among 54 Widal-positive patients, only five (9.3%) were confirmed by blood culture, while 49 (90.7%) were culture-negative.
analysis.methods: The study involved a retrospective audit of Widal test results and compared them with blood culture findings to assess diagnostic accuracy. It also referenced the limitations of blood culture and the challenges of implementing better diagnostics in low-resource settings.
analysis.main_results: An analysis showed that Widal performs poorly relative to other diagnostics and adds no incremental value when combined with better-performing rapid tests; notably, none of the best-performing diagnostic combinations included Widal.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the poor performance of Widal testing undermines accurate disease surveillance and contributes to the spread of antimicrobial resistance, highlighting the need for policy-driven changes in diagnostic practices.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Eliminating inaccurate diagnostics for enteric fever is essential for improving patient care, reducing inappropriate antibiotic use and advancing public health data reliability, particularly in regions with high disease burden.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and focus on a single tertiary hospital, which may not represent broader trends. The evidence is moderate, as it relies on existing data rather than prospective trials.

analysis.summary_en: This study argues for the elimination of the Widal test for diagnosing enteric fever in India due to its poor accuracy and contribution to antimicrobial resistance. A retrospective audit of 100 febrile children at a New Delhi hospital found that only 9.3% of Widal-positive cases were confirmed by blood culture, highlighting the test's high rate of false positives. The authors emphasize that inaccurate diagnostics hinder disease surveillance and appropriate treatment, leading to unnecessary antibiotic exposure and delayed care. They suggest that policy enforcement and integration of more reliable diagnostic methods, such as nucleic acid amplification tests, could improve outcomes. However, the study's limitations include its retrospective nature and limited geographic scope, which may affect the generalizability of its findings. The evidence is moderate, as it relies on existing data rather than new experimental results.

title: Epitope Tagging and Coimmunoprecipitation to Identify Viral Protein Interactors.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of traditional AP-MS methods by developing a more accurate strategy for identifying viral protein interactors in a physiologically relevant context. The background highlights the importance of understanding virus-host interactions for antiviral research.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study introduced an AP-MS strategy based on direct infection with an epitope-tagged chikungunya virus (CHIKV/myc-E2) to uncover new antiviral factors in CHIKV cellular reservoirs, specifically macrophages.
analysis.methods: The method involved designing and constructing a myc-tagged chikungunya virus using advanced multi-fragment assembly, preparing infectious myc-tagged virus stocks through in vitro transcription, and performing immunoprecipitation of the myc-tagged viral protein followed by mass spectrometry analysis of its interactome.
analysis.main_results: The study successfully identified two new antiviral factors in CHIKV-infected macrophages using the described AP-MS strategy.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as demonstrating the effectiveness of their novel AP-MS strategy in accurately identifying viral interactors in a physiologically relevant context, which provides a framework for future proteomic studies using tagged viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings offer a methodological advancement for studying virus-host interactions, which can inform future research on antiviral factors and potentially contribute to the development of targeted therapies for chikungunya virus infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to an abstract-only description of the method and its application, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of detailed results and statistical analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a novel AP-MS strategy for identifying chikungunya virus (CHIKV) protein interactors by directly infecting cells with an epitope-tagged CHIKV strain (CHIKV/myc-E2). The method involves constructing a myc-tagged virus through advanced multi-fragment assembly, preparing infectious virus stocks via in vitro transcription, and analyzing the interactome using immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry. The study successfully identified two new antiviral factors in CHIKV-infected macrophages, demonstrating the potential of this approach for future proteomic studies. The findings highlight the importance of using physiologically relevant contexts for accurate identification of viral interactors, which can inform antiviral research. However, the study is limited to an abstract-only description, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of detailed results and statistical analysis.

title: The consequence of simultaneous and sequential coinfections of Aedes aegypti with DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV on vector competence

analysis.research_question_and_background: Vector-borne diseases (VBD) caused by arboviruses represent a major public health threat in tropical regions. The study aimed to understand how coinfections with different arboviruses affect the transmission potential of mosquitoes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Brazil, focusing on Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. It examined the effects of simultaneous and sequential coinfections with DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV on vector competence.
analysis.methods: The researchers used Aedes aegypti mosquitoes to study the effects of coinfections with DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV. They analyzed infection rates, viral loads, and transmission efficiency through experimental exposure and subsequent testing.
analysis.main_results: At 7 days post-infection, DENV-1 infection rates and viral loads were significantly reduced compared with monoinfections, whereas DENV-2 showed increased viral loads in saliva. At 14 dpi, CHIKV infection rates were significantly reduced in both the CHIKV+DENV-1 and CHIKV+DENV-2 groups, with CHIKV viral loads reduced only in the CHIKV+DENV-2 group.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that simultaneous coinfection with CHIKV and DENV serotypes resulted in serotype-dependent outcomes, highlighting the complexity of arboviral interactions in mosquitoes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings emphasize the importance of considering different coinfection scenarios when evaluating vector competence and transmission risk in endemic settings, which can inform more effective surveillance and control strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, which may lack detailed experimental data. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the absence of comprehensive results and statistical analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the effects of simultaneous and sequential coinfections with DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV on the vector competence of Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. It highlights that coinfection outcomes are serotype-dependent, with DENV-1 and DENV-2 showing distinct responses to CHIKV. The findings suggest that different coinfection scenarios may influence transmission dynamics, which is important for understanding and managing vector-borne diseases in tropical regions. However, the study is based on abstract-only evidence, limiting the confidence in its conclusions.

title: Development of a Single Thermal Cycling Multiplex RT-qPCR Assay for Rapid Arbovirus Detection

analysis.research_question_and_background: The co-circulation of multiple arboviruses with similar clinical presentations poses a significant challenge for public health surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A diagnostic accuracy study was conducted in Salvador, Brazil, evaluating 254 prospective serum samples and 34 archived positive samples.
analysis.methods: The primers and probes for the assay were designed in silico, targeting highly conserved regions of Dengue (DENV), Zika (ZIKV), Chikungunya (CHIKV), Oropouche (OROV), and West Nile (WNV) viruses. The protocol was optimized in three reactions with a single thermal cycle, comprising a tetraplex reaction (DENV, CHIKV, ZIKV, and hRNAseP, an endogenous control) and two singleplex reactions (OROV and WNV).
analysis.main_results: In prospective analysis, the assay identified 45 DENV, 3 CHIKV, and 9 OROV-positive cases. Diagnostic accuracy for DENV and CHIKV was 96% (95% CI: 93.3–98.0%), successfully detecting four DENV cases missed by the reference standard. Incorporating OROV enabled the identification of nine cases that conventional triplex protocols would have overlooked.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This single-cycling multiplex RT-qPCR assay enhances epidemiological surveillance by expanding detection beyond traditional triplex targets to include OROV and WNV. This operational optimization reduces turnaround times and prevents the underdiagnosis of emerging arboviruses, serving as a robust diagnostic tool for endemic regions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This assay improves the detection of CHIKV and other arboviruses, aiding in the surveillance and management of arboviral diseases in endemic regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in a specific location and used a limited sample size, which may limit generalizability. The diagnostic accuracy for CHIKV was high, but the sample size was small, which may affect the robustness of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a single-cycling multiplex RT-qPCR assay for the simultaneous detection of five arboviruses, enhancing surveillance and reducing diagnostic delays. The assay showed high accuracy for DENV and CHIKV, identifying cases missed by conventional methods.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate and measure the long-distance relationship between the global Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) and local Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) transmission dynamics in Indonesia from January 2012 to December 2023 (n = 144 months). analysis.study_design_and_population: This study employed a quantitative associative time-series design within RStudio to evaluate the relationship between the global Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) and local Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) transmission dynamics in Indonesia from January 2012 to December 2023 (n = 144 months).
analysis.methods: Methodologically, a quantitative associative time-series design was employed within RStudio. The datasets exhibited non-normal distributions and raw non-stationarity, which were addressed through a first-order differencing transformation to achieve stationarity. The Cross-Correlation Function (CCF) was then calculated across an interaction window from Lag -6 to Lag +6 months.
analysis.main_results: The results revealed a highly dynamic double-peak epidemiological pattern, peaking in 2013 (15,324 cases) and 2023 (6,049 cases). A significant, optimal positive cross-correlation emerged at Lag -6 (r=0.1246), confirming an asymmetric teleconnection where an increase in the ONI preceding the current period by six months directly drives increased Chikungunya outbreaks in Indonesia.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as confirming an asymmetric teleconnection where an increase in the ONI preceding the current period by six months directly drives increased Chikungunya outbreaks in Indonesia, providing a vital baseline for climate-based Early Warning Systems. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of climate-based Early Warning Systems for Chikungunya outbreaks in Indonesia, enhancing surveillance and public health preparedness. analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study design limitations include the use of non-stationary time series data, which may introduce biases. title: Retinal manifestations of neglected tropical diseases.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review addresses the timely need for ophthalmologists to recognize the retinal manifestations of NTDs, as these conditions now appear in developed nations where clinicians may have limited prior exposure.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of recent findings on retinal manifestations of NTDs, with no explicit mention of databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Modern multimodal imaging has revealed distinct retinal patterns that are frequently seen in NTDs.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not report controversies or evidence gaps related to retinal manifestations of chikungunya virus.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Summary Recognition of retinal manifestations is crucial for NTD diagnosis and management. Collaborative care with infectious disease specialists and utilization of appropriate diagnostic modalities facilitate optimal outcomes and prevent vision loss while addressing broader public health implications.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on the retinal manifestations of chikungunya virus and other neglected tropical diseases (NTDs). It highlights the increasing prevalence of NTDs in non-endemic regions due to global migration, travel, and climate change. The review emphasizes the importance of recognizing retinal patterns associated with NTDs, particularly through modern imaging techniques. It underscores the need for ophthalmologists to maintain high clinical suspicion based on patient travel history and systemic symptoms. The review also stresses the value of collaborative care with infectious disease specialists and the use of appropriate diagnostic tools to prevent vision loss and address public health implications. However, the evidence does not report specific controversies or gaps related to chikungunya virus retinal manifestations.

title: Indigofera suffruticosa as a Source of Anti-Arboviral Phytoconstituents: Bioguided Fractionation, Isolation of 3-O-β-D-Glucosyl-β-Sitosterol, and In Vitro Evaluation Against ZIKV, CHIKV, and MAYV

analysis.research_question_and_background: Arboviruses transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, including Zika (ZIKV), Chikungunya (CHIKV), and Mayaro (MAYV) viruses, lack approved antiviral therapies. This study aimed to identify potential anti-arboviral compounds from Indigofera suffruticosa Mill.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study evaluated the cytotoxicity and antiviral activity of ethanolic extracts and fractions from stems and leaves of Indigofera suffruticosa Mill. The study was conducted in vitro using Vero cells as the host.
analysis.methods: Cytotoxicity was assessed by the MTT assay in MRC-5 and Vero cells, and antiviral activity was determined in simultaneous treatment-infection assays in Vero cells. Extracts were obtained by cold maceration and partitioned into chloroform, ethyl acetate, and aqueous methanol fractions. Bioguided fractionation was used to isolate the active principles.
analysis.main_results: The stem ethanolic extract showed potent anti-ZIKV activity (EC50 = 29.43 ± 1.43 μg/mL; SI > 13.59). The chloroform fraction displayed broad-spectrum efficacy, with EC50 = 89.48 ± 2.70 μg/mL (ZIKV; SI > 4.47), 37.05 ± 2.26 μg/mL (CHIKV; SI > 10.80), and 42.39 ± 3.60 μg/mL (MAYV; SI > 9.44).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified 3-O-β-D-glucosyl-β-sitosterol as a compound with selective anti-alphavirus activity against CHIKV and MAYV, but not ZIKV, suggesting that additional constituents may be responsible for the anti-flaviviral effect.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Indigofera suffruticosa is a promising source of broad-spectrum anti-arboviral agents, supporting further bioassay-guided isolation and mechanistic studies for potential therapeutic applications.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to in vitro evaluations, and the findings do not account for in vivo efficacy or clinical relevance. The evidence is moderate as it is based on laboratory assays without human or animal trial data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential of Indigofera suffruticosa Mill as a source of anti-arboviral compounds against Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and Mayaro virus (MAYV). The researchers evaluated the cytotoxicity and antiviral activity of ethanolic extracts and fractions from the plant's stems and leaves. They found that the stem extract showed potent anti-ZIKV activity, while the chloroform fraction demonstrated broad-spectrum efficacy against all three viruses. Bioguided fractionation led to the isolation of 3-O-β-D-glucosyl-β-sitosterol, which exhibited selective anti-alphavirus activity against CHIKV and MAYV but was inactive against ZIKV. These findings suggest that Indigofera suffruticosa may be a valuable source of anti-arboviral agents, warranting further research into its bioactive components and mechanisms. However, the study was limited to in vitro evaluations, and the results do not provide evidence for in vivo or clinical applications.

title: Microemulsion-based delivery of peppermint essential oil as a sustainable strategy for Aedes aegypti control

analysis.research_question_and_background: Arboviral diseases such as dengue, Zika, and chikungunya remain major public health challenges worldwide. In the absence of broadly effective antiviral therapies and considering the limitations of current vaccination strategies, vector control remains the primary approach for reducing disease transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study investigated the chemical composition, larvicidal activity, and microemulsion-based formulation of Mentha piperita L. essential oil against Aedes aegypti larvae. The free essential oil exhibited concentration-dependent larvicidal activity against Aedes aegypti, with an LC 50 of 175.7 μg/mL and complete larval mortality at 250 μg/mL.
analysis.methods: The chemical composition of the essential oil was determined by gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS). A pseudoternary phase diagram was constructed to identify suitable microemulsion regions, and selected formulations were characterized according to droplet size, polydispersity index (PDI), and short-term physical stability.
analysis.main_results: GC–MS analysis identified 14 compounds representing nearly 100% of the essential oil composition, with menthol (50.17%) and menthone (23.02%) as the predominant constituents. Among the tested formulations, PME-05 was selected as the most promising formulation for further development because it achieved complete larval mortality while containing only 5% peppermint essential oil and exhibited the lowest PDI (0.06 ± 0.007), indicating a highly homogeneous dispersed system.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results support the use of microemulsion technology as a suitable delivery system for Mentha piperita L. essential oil, facilitating its dispersion and application in aqueous environments while retaining its larvicidal activity. The developed formulation represents a promising platform for the application of botanical larvicides in mosquito control.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that microemulsion-based delivery systems could offer a sustainable and effective method for controlling Aedes aegypti, which is a vector for chikungunya and other arboviruses. This could inform future research and development of eco-friendly vector control strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Further studies are needed to evaluate long-term physicochemical stability, residual activity, effects on non-target organisms, and performance under semi-field and field conditions. The evidence is moderate as it is based on laboratory findings and does not include field validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the use of microemulsion-based delivery of peppermint essential oil as a sustainable strategy for controlling Aedes aegypti, a vector for chikungunya and other arboviruses. The research highlights the chemical composition of the essential oil, demonstrating its larvicidal activity against Aedes aegypti larvae. The study identifies PME-05 as a promising formulation due to its high efficacy and stability. The findings suggest that microemulsions could be a viable platform for botanical larvicides in mosquito control. However, the study is limited to laboratory conditions, and further research is needed to assess long-term stability and field performance. The results provide a novel approach to vector control, potentially supporting the development of eco-friendly alternatives to synthetic insecticides.

title: B-144 Performance of IgM ELISA and RT-PCR for Oropouche Virus diagnosis: defining the diagnostic window

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to define the diagnostic window for Oropouche virus (OROV) by evaluating the relationship between days post-symptom onset (DPSO), anti-IgM ratio (ELISA), and RT-PCR results, given the overlap of symptoms with other arboviruses such as dengue and chikungunya.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study evaluated serum samples (n=180) from patients in Espirito Santo State (Brazil) presenting symptoms consistent with arboviruses, with sampling concentrated in the 5–7 DPSO window representing 75% of the cohort.
analysis.methods: Serum samples were tested using an in-house RT-PCR targeting the S gene of OROV and an indirect IgM ELISA (EUROIMMUN), with results expressed as ratio. The diagnostic window was analyzed in relation to DPSO, with specific strata for 10 days (n=18) and other timeframes.
analysis.main_results: Overall, 50.6% (91/180) of samples tested positive for OROV in at least one assay, with 14.3% (13/91) being double-positive, 46.2% (42/91) RT-PCR positive only, and 39.6% (36/91) IgM positive only. In the 10 days strata, IgM reactivity was 48% (12/25) and 44.4% (8/18), while RT-PCR positivity was 40% (10/25) and 22.2% (4/18).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reinforce the temporal complementarity between RT-PCR and IgM ELISA for OROV diagnosis, highlighting that a significant proportion of RT-PCR positive cases remain IgM negative for up to 7 days, and vice versa, while IgM reactivity increases substantially from 8 days onwards.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide critical insights for diagnostic strategies in clinical scenarios with a longer duration of symptoms, emphasizing the importance of using IgM serology in later stages when viral load decreases and RT-PCR sensitivity declines.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is limited to abstract-only data, and the sampling was concentrated in the 5–7 DPSO window, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of detailed statistical analysis and the potential for bias in the selected cohort.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the diagnostic window for Oropouche virus (OROV) by analyzing the relationship between days post-symptom onset (DPSO), anti-IgM ratio (ELISA), and RT-PCR results. It found that 50.6% of samples tested positive for OROV in at least one assay, with RT-PCR being more effective in early stages and IgM ELISA gaining importance in later phases. The results highlight the temporal complementarity of these methods for OROV diagnosis, suggesting that IgM serology is more clinically useful in prolonged symptomatic cases. However, the study's evidence is limited to abstract-only data, and the focus on the 5–7 DPSO window may restrict generalizability, resulting in moderate confidence in the findings.
